name: Browns Range Heavy Rare Earths Project

value.note: Average steady-state xenotime concentrate at ~25% TREO (Table 1, p.7); contains ~4,350 tpa TREO of which ~10.7% is Dy/Tb
Total dry concentrate over the 11-year LOM, containing 45,000 t TREO (Table 1, p.7; Table 9, p.20)
Dy2O3 contained in concentrate over LOM (Table 9, p.20); separated downstream at Eneabba, not produced as oxide at site
Tb4O7 contained in concentrate over LOM (Table 9, p.20); separated downstream at Eneabba, not produced as oxide at site

description: 100%-owned by Northern Minerals. Open-pit then underground (sublevel caving) mining of the Wolverine deposit, with on-site crushing, grinding, magnetic separation and flotation producing a ~25% TREO xenotime concentrate, trucked by road to Iluka's Eneabba refinery. DFS: A$592M pre-production capital, 11-year LOM, ~84% TREO recovery. FID subject to funding; construction ~26 months from financial close, targeting completion Q4 2027 and ramp-up in 2028. Dy/Tb ~70% of basket value.

name: Wimmera Project

value.note: UNVERIFIED: ~15 ktpa rare-earth concentrate to Eneabba for 25+ years, per Iluka refinery feed scenarios cited in the v0 brief. Not stated in the 2025 Annual Report, which says only 'potential multi-decade source of light and heavy rare earths'. Not a committed production plan.

description: Mining and beneficiation of a fine-grained heavy mineral sands ore body in western Victoria for potential long-term supply of rare earths (monazite/xenotime: Nd/Pr plus Dy/Tb) and zircon. In definitive feasibility study; Environment Effects Statement being prepared for submission to the Victorian Government in 2026; detailed engineering began 2025 with WSP as major engineering provider (Integrated Owner's Team). Flowsheet successfully tested with finished zircon produced (~40% of zircon suitable for ceramics, markets identified for ~60%). Resource increase announced January 2026 following additional exploration and modelling. ~A$10M of 2025 feasibility spend covered Wimmera, Tutunup and other deposits. Iluka expects Wimmera (with Eneabba) to be operational in the long term (2040-2050).

name: Fingerboards Critical Minerals Project

value.note: Containing roughly 14,000 tpa of xenotime and monazite rare-earth minerals
Heavy rare-earth oxides including Dy and Tb, contained in product
Light rare-earth oxides including Nd and Pr, contained in product

description: Development-stage mineral-sands project at the Glenaladale deposit. Heavy mineral concentrate would be processed further in the Northern Territory or Western Australia; the specific downstream refinery is not publicly established.

name: Serra Verde Pela Ema Operation

value.note: Rare-earth oxide equivalent contained in mixed rare-earth carbonate; company target by end of 2027

description: Integrated mining and processing operation in commercial production since 2024, producing a mixed rare-earth carbonate with Dy, Tb, Nd and Pr — the first scaled producer outside Asia of all four magnet rare earths.

name: Eneabba Rare Earths Stockpile (Phases 1-2)

value.note: Maximum refinery plant feed rate of 18 ktpa CONTAINED REO (before recovery losses) when processing the Eneabba stockpile, per Iluka Investor Briefing Day 5 May 2025 as cited in AR25 p.57; not concentrate mass. Corresponding REO output rate 16.0 ktpa.

description: Iluka's existing stockpile of rare-earth-bearing monazite and xenotime at Eneabba, WA (a by-product of historical mineral-sands mining), with Phase 1 screening and Phase 2 concentrating plant already built (A$50M deployed). Described by Iluka as the highest-grade rare earths operation globally; valued at A$1,270M as an equity-like contribution to the refinery (FID 2022). No mining required. Provides the refinery's initial feed for an indicative nine years; replenished from Iluka's Jacinth-Ambrosia and Cataby mineral-sands operations. AR25: the Rare Earths segment comprises the refinery plus Phases 1 and 2; Iluka's 2026 LTIP targets securing at least 8 kt contained NdPr (or Dy/Tb equivalent) of additional feedstock beyond the monazite stockpile. Tonnage and REO assemblage of the stockpile not disclosed.

name: Kangankunde Rare Earths Project
description: Rare-earth deposit in Malawi being developed by Lindian Resources; described by Iluka as 'a major source of neodymium and praseodymium'. Included here only as a contracted Eneabba feedstock (light rare earths) - it is not a Dy/Tb alternative to Browns Range. Stage and status inferred from Iluka's description of Lindian as 'developing' the deposit; no Lindian disclosure has been reviewed.
